critical_errors.issue: Gubler--Rabinoff Proposition 5.1 is stated for smooth strictly analytic curves, and its explicit coefficient computation is made after passage to an algebraically closed field and a formal model with reduced special fiber. The lifted curve C is only shown to be irreducible and an ordinary local complete intersection; the proof does not show that C is rig-smooth/geometrically regular. Over an arbitrary possibly imperfect K, ordinary regularity of O_{C,z} does not imply geometric regularity. Nor is any descent or general model-current formula supplied that proves, for the possibly nonreduced formal closure, the asserted coefficient m_z deg(L|_{Gamma'}) with a strictly positive and correctly normalized multiplicity. Thus the cited result cannot be applied as written, and the negative atom needed for the contradiction is unproved. Chambert--Loir--Ducros Corollary 18.8.8 does not repair this step because its stated equivalence concerns integral PL metrics, not the arbitrary real-PL metric used here.

repair_hints: [pi_f71271c9a6450fcb5b581304] Either prove that the lifted curve is rig-smooth near z and then give a precise base-change/descent argument reducing the coefficient calculation to the smooth reduced-model case, or cite and apply a general model-current formula valid for singular curves, arbitrary complete K, real coefficients, and nonreduced formal models. Define the multiplicity explicitly and verify that the formula and projection formula give a strictly positive factor times deg(L|_{Gamma'}).
